chapters.title: New City, Feeling Lonely After Work
chapters.futureNote: I moved cities recently. I feel lonely after work.
chapters.confirmedGoal: Find regular companionship through shared interests.

contributors.approvedSummary: At first I asked everyone what I should do about my relationship. I got completely different answers. Some were kind, some felt like instructions. I stopped asking for a verdict and asked one trusted friend to listen while I worked out what mattered to me. I was still uncertain afterward, but I could hear my own thinking again.

I love my parents, but every call became a question about what I was going to do. I started avoiding them, which made me feel worse. Eventually I told my sister I could talk about how I was doing, but I wasn't ready for everyone to vote on my decision. It didn't solve everything. It made our conversations less exhausting.
For me, boundaries weren't enough on their own. Distance and professional support mattered more. Nobody else's timeline fit mine.

milestones.title: Every question felt like a demand for an answer
milestones.whatHappened: When everyone asked me what I'd decided, I felt that I owed them an immediate answer.
milestones.whatIActuallyTried: I spent a lot of time asking other people what I should do.
milestones.whatDidNotHelp: I also tried reading many anonymous opinions, but I found that overwhelming.

milestones.title: Separating my worries from other people's expectations
milestones.whatHappened: I wanted space to think before another person offered a verdict.
milestones.whatIActuallyTried: I wrote down which worries were mine and which came from other people's expectations. I asked a trusted friend for a conversation without advice.
milestones.whatHelped: My friend listened without deciding for me.

milestones.title: Clearer about what I needed, not the relationship outcome
milestones.whatHappened: I became clearer about what to ask for: time to think and someone who would listen.
milestones.whatIActuallyTried: I kept reflecting on what mattered to me.
milestones.whatHelped: I could hear my own thinking again.
milestones.whatDidNotHelp: I did not suddenly know what to do about the relationship.

milestones.whatDidNotHelp: I could not use another person's timeline as my own.

peerQuestionDemo.questionText: When you didn't want to disappoint your family, how did you figure out what you wanted before listening to everyone else's opinions?

response.label: Prepared illustrative reply
response.text: I didn't know at first. I kept asking people what they'd do, and their answers made me more unsure. What helped was writing down the one question I wanted to answer for myself, then asking a friend to listen without giving me a verdict. I still had a hard conversation with my family afterward. It wasn't a quick fix.

sampleApprovedInsight: I want to figure out what matters to me before asking others for answers.
